key_insight: A one-dimensional Quantum Lattice Boltzmann Method reproduces expected advection–diffusion dynamics on quantum hardware, but collision and streaming operations remain major scalability bottlenecks.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark identifies practical hardware and algorithmic barriers to using quantum-native methods for fluid simulation rather than demonstrating an advantage over classical CFD.
method: Encode the advection–diffusion problem in quantum amplitudes.
Apply a BGK-type collision operator and periodic-boundary streaming.
Reconstruct macroscopic density from computational-basis samples instead of full state tomography.
evidence_signal: Tests on three IBM Quantum hardware systems evaluate transpiled two-qubit gate counts, circuit depth, runtime, maximum absolute error, and RMSE.
watch_item: Results are limited to a one-dimensional benchmark on noisy hardware; scalability to larger or more complex flows remains unproven.
paper_title: Benchmarking One-Dimensional Quantum Lattice Boltzmann Methods on Quantum Hardware
